newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cenbank rev repo was to steer rates-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Polish cenbank rev repo was to steer rates-dealers.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's (NBP) one-day reverse repo operation on Wednesday was meant to show traders where the NBP wanted to see one-day rates rather than drain money from the market, dealers said.

The NBP drained only 21 million zlotys from the system through the operation setting the rate at 21.30 percent after banks bid for 113 million zlotys against a 300 million zloty offer. It was the first one-day operation since August 26.
Earlier this month the central bank reiterated it would welcome higher real interest rates to curb fast growing credit.
"The NBP wanted to show where it saw the one-day rate...in line with earlier statements in which it talked about higher real interest rates," said Elwir Swietochowski from PBI SA.
The NBP's benchmark 14-day reverse repo rate was last at 19.16 percent on November 28. O/N rates rose to 21.30/22.50 after the operation from 20.50/23.00 percent previously.
"This was (aimed at) raising the market rate without raising the base rates, exactly what NBP promised to do," said Andrzej Ladko, chief dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The average accepted rate was also 21.30 percent, which dealers said suggested the NBP accepted only the edge bid, refraining at present from a larger rate rise.
"The NBP could have raised the one-day rate by more, it accepted only the edge of bids," Handlowy's Ladko said.
"The growth in the intervention rate is limited because the NBP cannot pay for the funds it withdraws from the system more than the rate at which it gives credits," he added.
Dealers said the 1-day reverse repo rate did not affect tomorrow/next rates, which traded above 21.30 percent before and after the operation at 22.1/24.1 percent.
Analysts said the central bank could now also raise its 14-day maximum drainage rate.
Some dealers said the NBP raised the one-day rate only because of a short-term liquidity boom in December, amid generally high rates due to increased outflows.
"I do not treat today's operation as an indication of anything. For me it is nothing more than a one-day reverse repo with a value date on December 12," said one dealer at a foreign bank here.
